en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eleventh Chapter
In the Discourse on Concentration:
Is the continuity of mind concentration? Yes.
Is the past continuum of consciousness concentration?
One should not say so …pe… Is the continuum of consciousness concentration?
“Yes.
“Is the future continuity of consciousness concentration?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is the continuity of consciousness (cittasantati) concentration (samādhi)? Yes.
But is it not the case that the past has ceased and the future is unborn?
“Yes.
“If the past has ceased and the future is unborn, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘The continuity of consciousness is concentration.’”
Is concentration momentary, lasting for a single moment of consciousness? Yes.
Is one who possesses eye-consciousness absorbed in jhāna? No.
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … one possessing ear-consciousness … [and so on] … one possessing nose-consciousness …
One possessing tongue-consciousness … one possessing body-consciousness …pe… one possessing unwholesome consciousness …pe…
One possessing a mind accompanied by lust …pe… one possessing a mind accompanied by hatred …pe… one possessing a mind accompanied by delusion …pe…
Is one who possesses a mind accompanied by lack of moral dread (anottappa) said to have attained meditative absorption (samāpanna)?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is the continuity of consciousness (cittasantati) concentration (samādhi)?
“Yes.
“Is the continuity of unwholesome consciousness concentration?
One should not say so … [and so on] …
Accompanied by lust … [and so on] … accompanied by hatred … [and so on] … accompanied by delusion … [and so on].
Is the mental continuum accompanied by lack of moral dread "concentration"?
One should not say so …pe… It should not be said.
“Is the continuity of consciousness (cittasantati) concentration (samādhi)?
— Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Friends, Nigaṇṭhas, I am indeed able, without moving my body and without speaking a word, to dwell experiencing exclusive happiness for seven days and nights.
Is this a genuine sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, the continuity of consciousness is concentration.
The discussion on concentration is finished.
